texts.preamble: Natwar Bardhan vs State Of Bihar on 10 January, 2017 Author: Rongon Mukhopadhyay Bench: Rongon Mukhopadhyay Criminal Revision No. 272 of 1999 (R) In the matter of an application under Section 397 and 401 of the Code of Criminal Procedure --- Natwar Bardhan son of Late Krishna Chandra Bardhan resident of village Pupunki, Ps Chas (M), District Bokaro ... ... Petitioner Versus The State of Bihar ... ... Opposite Party --- For the Petitioner : Mr. A. K. Sahani, Advocate
texts.arguments: It has also been submitted that no charge has been framed under Sections 16(i) (a) (ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act. He further submits that out of the sentence of 3 months, the petitioner has remained in custody for 4 days. It appears from the allegation that the tea shop of the petitioner was inspected and at the time when the inspection was made, it was found that the licence which was produced by the petitioner has lapsed more than 3 years back. Three prosecution witnesses have been examined in course of trial who supported the prosecution case and since the petitioner was found to be running a shop without a valid licence, the petitioner was convicted for the offence punishable under Sections 16(i) (a) (ii) of Natwar Bardhan vs State Of Bihar on 10 January, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17507236/ 1 the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and was sentenced to undergo S.I. for 6 months. Since the allegation made in the complaint was substantiated in course of trial as the petitioner was running the tea stall without there being a valid licence, no interference is necessitated in the impugned judgment.
